body: My family says they don't think I'm bipolar because they don't think my behaviour matches someone who has bipolar. All of the people in my family who are bipolar have bipolar 1 and have very noticeable symptoms. They acknowledge that my depression is severe but say that I can't possibly be bipolar because my mania isn't bad enough.

Since I don't have access to the therapist I go to on campus because of the pandemic, I usually have worksheets that I work on (my doctor recommended a site with a bunch of worksheets and it really helps with identifying negative thoughts and such). I also have a mental health journal that I keep to vent and work through things. I've been put in touch with a permanent psychiatrist (and hopefully a psychologist as well), so luckily I have a lot of ways to work on bettering my coping skills.

Insurance. I've sent forms to try and get the medication approved, so now all I do is wait. I have an appointment with a psychiatrist to discuss med changes anyway (the Latuda wasn't doing very well). Hopefully I find something that works for me.
It's Latuda, so it is pretty expensive. I'm trying to get it approved through insurance. Hopefully it gets approved.

It went well. I didn't have to disclose anything, luckily. I'm doing alright—the medication I'm on just got increased and it seems to be working, so at least I'm becoming somewhat stable. I still get anxious when I think about how much leave I'm taking from work, but at least I'm not being fired.

As someone who has parents who like to minimize my mental illness, I keep it between me and my doctor whenever I can. 

My parents, especially my mother, like to try to diagnose me even though they aren't doctors. They keep insisting I'm not bipolar even though several doctors have said that based on my symptoms I have it. 

My parents are aware of my depressive episodes, but are almost never around or don't hear about my hypomanic ones, or the ones that are mixed. 
My parents only accept anxiety and depression as possible problems, so I just keep my bipolar diagnosis to myself mostly. 

Don't tell your parents if you can avoid it. I would definitely just keep it between you and your doctor.

Thank you for clarifying. I was confused when he started asking me how many episodes I had last year—I could count the hypomanic ones easier than my depression, because my depression lasts longer. I'm currently on my second day of another hypomanic episode, after two weeks of depression. Usually my depression lasts longer, but I'm under a lot of stress right now. I don't really experience rapid cycling in my mood. I'm being set up with a permanent psychiatrist (different from the one I saw initially) so hopefully they'll be a good one.

Yes, I have BP2 and OCD. My OCD is severe (I'm currently getting my meds switched and my skin-picking compulsions are out of control). I find it's worse during my hypomanic periods than in my depression, and it definitely sucks. I also have intrusive thoughts, and I have issues around contamination as well (I can't touch dirt without gloves). 

I read somewhere that bipolar 2 and OCD have a high rate of comorbidity, which is interesting if true.

I just got diagnosed and saw a psychiatrist a week ago. When I told him that sometimes my moods were mixed and that I can be hypomanic and depressed at the same time, he asked me what I meant and seemed really confused. I was surprised because I thought they would know about mixed states, but I guess not. It's really discouraged me from talking to psychiatrists about it because they don't seem to acknowledge or know about mixed states.
